sources.entry: BeardedSpice - Control web players and supported apps with your keyboard media keys. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/beardedspice/beardedspice) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]
BeardedSpice - Control web based media players with the media keys found on Mac keyboards.

summary.one_liner: BeardedSpice is a macOS menu bar app that lets the Mac keyboard's media keys control web-based music and video players and some native apps.
summary.what_it_does: BeardedSpice runs in the macOS menu bar and routes media keys to web players opened in Chrome, Safari, or Vivaldi, including many music and podcast sites such as SoundCloud, YouTube, Spotify (Web), and Pandora. You pick which site to control from the menu bar icon. It also supports native apps such as iTunes, Spotify, VLC, VOX, Downcast, and TIDAL Desktop. A "Smart" mode tries to guess which tab to control, and default keyboard shortcuts (⌘+F8, F6, F10, F11) set the active player, focus it, toggle favorites, and show track info. Users can remap media keys for non-Apple keyboards and enable or disable individual site handlers. Media strategies (per-site JavaScript templates) can be exported and imported as .bsstrategy files, and an update check looks for new strategies.
use_cases: Control YouTube or SoundCloud playback with Mac media keys
Pause or skip music in Spotify or iTunes from the keyboard
Use media keys with a non-Apple keyboard
Set up keyboard shortcuts to toggle favorites or show track info
Control music playing in a browser tab while working in other apps
how_to_run: Download the latest release from the project's releases page (macOS 10.10 or greater required)
Open your supported media site in Chrome, Safari, or Vivaldi
Click the BeardedSpice menu bar icon and select the site to control
For Safari (9.1.1 or later), enable the developer preference as described in the README guide
stack: Objective-C (native macOS app, per README contribution notes)
notable: Media keys control many web players in Chrome, Safari, and Vivaldi without a separate app per site
Smart mode auto-selects the currently playing tab
Shareable .bsstrategy files let users exchange per-site controllers
caveats: Safari needs a developer preference enabled
Smart mode is marked as a work-in-progress and not yet available on all sites
